thread_analysis.thread_summary: This thread (June–August 2025) covers the full lifecycle of a Bluetooth SIG certification for [COMPANY] Topre's new R4H series Bluetooth HID keyboard family (4 models: R4HA, R4HB, R4HC, R4HD). Key topics: (1) Quote scope clarification - HOGP test is mandatory for a keyboard certification to be meaningful (without it, the certification covers only 'profile-less product'); (2) Post-July 2024 cascade profile requirements - HOGP now mandates BAS, DIS, HIDS testing (4 profiles total, ¥400,000), whereas the 2021 registration required only HOGP; (3) Representative model selection - only 1 of 4 keyboard models is tested, others added to Product List; (4) PTS test FAIL troubleshooting - Connectable Mode not set, and multi-slot BT keyboard with per-slot BT addresses causing address mismatch between setup and execution; (5) PTS FAIL root cause - firmware missing BAS Battery Level, DIS PnP ID and other GATT characteristics required by post-July 2024 rules; (6) Bluetooth test independence from parallel WHQL certification. The thread also included quote evolution: initial ¥400,000 (proxy + CF, no profile test based on empty BLE Profile field in RFQ), then ¥800,000 after customer requested HOGP test inclusion (4 profiles + proxy + CF), then updated to include SIG payment remittance proxy.
all_questions_found: Can we get Bluetooth SIG certification without HOGP profile testing? What does the certification cover if we skip HOGP?
Why does a new HOGP keyboard registration now require BAS, DIS, HIDS testing in addition to HOGP, when our 2021 registration only needed HOGP?
PTS test is showing FAIL results - the DUT is not connecting. What is the cause, and how does having 4 Bluetooth pairing slots affect PTS testing?
BAS, DIS, HIDS PTS items are failing even though HOGP passed. What is missing from our firmware?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Two policy-level changes define this thread: (1) Post-July 2024 HOGP cascade requirement: BAS, DIS, HIDS are now mandatory for HOGP HID Device registration (芋づる式). The HOGP spec itself is unchanged; the SIG registration system's ICS consistency checker now properly enforces these dependencies, which were previously missed (check rule gap). (2) Certification scope: End Product registration without profile testing gives a 'profile-less product' certification - this does not cover HOGP and is meaningless for a keyboard. Technically two PTS failure modes emerged during testing: connection failure from non-Connectable Mode, and address mismatch from multi-slot operation. Root cause of the 9 FAIL items was that the firmware team implemented the same BT profile set as the 2021 keyboard, unaware that BAS Battery Level, DIS PnP ID, and other GATT characteristics became mandatory in 2024.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: For HOGP HID device registration under post-July 2024 rules, always quote 4-profile test scope (HOGP+BAS+DIS+HIDS). The certification scope must match the product's actual implementation - profile-less Core registration is not suitable for a keyboard. PTS test failures must be triaged as: (a) test execution issues (Connectable Mode, address mismatch) vs. (b) product implementation gaps (missing GATT characteristics). Implementation gaps require firmware changes; execution issues require test procedure adjustment.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Quoting only HOGP (as in 2021) for a post-2024 registration would result in an incomplete quote and registration rejection. Skipping profile testing entirely produces a meaningless certification for a keyboard product. Misdiagnosing firmware gaps as test execution problems leads to repeated failed test cycles without resolving the underlying issue.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For Bluetooth HID keyboard products: (1) Always quote 4 profiles for HOGP HID Device since post-July 2024 (HOGP + BAS + DIS + HIDS); (2) Explicitly explain to customers that skipping HOGP test produces only a 'profile-less product' certification; (3) Proactively communicate to the customer's SW development team at project start that BAS/DIS/HIDS GATT characteristics are now mandatory - early awareness prevents late-stage firmware surprises; (4) For multi-slot BT keyboards, brief the test engineer on address lock procedures for PTS testing; (5) Always confirm Bluetooth test failures are independent of parallel certifications (WHQL, etc.) to keep teams working without cross-blocking.
